title: Error objects and custom errors
learningObjectives: Explain error objects and custom errors and diagnose or handle JavaScript errors safely.

understand.concept: JavaScript Error objects represent exceptional conditions and commonly provide name, message, and stack properties. Custom error classes can extend Error to represent domain-specific failures. Error messages should be useful for developers but should not expose secrets or internal details to end users.
understand.whyItMatters: Typed errors help distinguish expected failure categories and support consistent handling. Preserve the original cause when wrapping errors where supported and useful.
understand.analogy: An Error object is a report describing what went wrong; a custom error adds a category that fits the application's domain.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript parsing, execution, and exception propagation follow language and runtime rules.

explain.narrative: The function throws a custom ValidationError when the name is empty, and the catch block can identify the error type.

examples.code: <script>class ValidationError extends Error{constructor(message){super(message);this.name='ValidationError';}}function requireName(name){if(!name)throw new ValidationError('Name is required');return name;}try{console.log(requireName(''));}catch(error){console.log(error.name,error.message);}</script>
examples.explanation: The function throws a custom ValidationError when the name is empty, and the catch block can identify the error type.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page demonstrates the error, stack, or handled result described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a custom error for an invalid lesson ID. Throw it when input fails validation and handle it separately from an unrelated runtime error.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example with a deliberate error or invalid input. Diagnose it using developer tools and provide useful, non-sensitive feedback.
hints: Separate syntax, runtime, and logic errors.
Read the first relevant application frame in a stack trace.
Do not silently swallow exceptions or expose secrets.

questions.prompt: What should a custom JavaScript error class usually extend?
questions.explanation: Custom error classes commonly extend the built-in Error class.

questions.prompt: What is a good error-handling practice?
options: Handle errors at meaningful boundaries and give safe feedback
Expose full stack traces and secrets to users
questions.answer: Handle errors at meaningful boundaries and give safe feedback
questions.explanation: Good error handling supports debugging while protecting users from sensitive internal details.
